errors: "39 of 41 ... under 5 seconds" is not established; the facts say most were under 5 seconds.
"2 index builds over 2 minutes ... outlast the probes" does not establish that both exceeded the 180-second liveness limit.
"Old pods keep serving" assumes the migration does not disrupt database traffic or compatibility.
"Under it, location doesn't matter; over it, entrypoint repeats INC-212" overstates both the absence of other benefits and the certainty of an identical outage.
R01.note: It explains the observed failure thoroughly, but turns limited timing evidence into categorical rules.

errors: "The other 39 took under 5 seconds" is not established.
"A slow migration means no healthy pods" assumes no existing serving pods remain during rollout.
"The old pods keep serving traffic" assumes database availability and compatibility during the migration.
"The cheaper alternative" is not supported by an implementation or cost comparison.
"Still blocks all three pods" is not established for every rollout.
R02.note: It offers actionable alternatives and admits uncertainty about the new migration, but adds substantial unasked discussion and unsupported rollout assumptions.

errors: "39 of 41 ... sub-5s" is not established.
"The two that weren't are the ones that hurt" invents an adverse outcome for the other slow migration.
"Migration runs to completion regardless of duration" is an unsupported guarantee.
"The 2-minute index migrations stop being dangerous" ignores database disruption and other failure causes.
"Pods crash-looping against a half-migrated schema and serving errors" is not in the evidence.
"~10 lines of YAML" is an invented implementation estimate.
"Bump ... thresholds so 180s > worst-case migration" contradicts the known 250-second migration and does not describe raising the limit correctly.
"The next 4-minute index build is still three concurrent restarts away" does not follow after raising the liveness limit.
R03.note: Its concrete incident explanation is undermined by invented details, absolute guarantees, and a contradictory alternative.

errors: "Your schema change is the kind of migration that can repeat it" invents the new migration's characteristics.
"How often this will happen ... about 1 in 20" treats migrations exceeding 120 seconds as evidence of failures at 180 seconds and as a future frequency.
"Works fine now ... true for about 95%" is not established by the timing distribution.
"Running pods keep serving" assumes database availability and compatibility.
"A migration over 180s takes all three pods down at once" overstates what is guaranteed for future rollouts.
"Outage lasts as long as the migration plus the restart cycles" is not an established duration rule.
"A one-line change" is an unverified implementation estimate.
"A plain column add (under 5s)" assumes an operation's duration without inspecting it.
R04.note: It supplies useful incident context but is repetitive and makes an unsupported claim about the current schema change.

errors: "When one runs longer [than 2 minutes] ... takes the orders API down" confuses the readiness timing with the 180-second restart limit.
"39 took under 5 seconds" is not established.
"Any migration in that slow group is where the current setup fails" is not established.
"Has no health checks" is an unverified proposed Job configuration, not an inherent Job property.
"Nothing kills it halfway and nothing waits on the lock" is an unsupported guarantee.
"Any migration over 2 minutes repeats INC-212" uses the wrong threshold and guarantees an identical incident.
"Likely to be in the slow group" is not established from two index builds without table or migration details.
R05.note: Its deciding rule uses the wrong timeout, so the otherwise concrete explanation would lead the user to misclassify migrations.

errors: "Existing pods keep serving" assumes the migration preserves their database access and compatibility.
R06.note: It gives the benefit, the failure mechanism, and the incident's magnitude concisely, with only an unstated assumption about continued service.

R07.note: It connects the recommendation to the actual restart deadline and explicitly limits the claim to the observed failure mechanism.

errors: "39 fast migrations" is not established.
"A process Kubernetes won't kill" is an unsupported guarantee.
"It still beats the cost" asserts a cost comparison without establishing it.
"Deploys get slower by the migration's duration" ignores that migrations already delay startup today.
"Roughly 1 deploy in 20 is exposed" conflates exceeding 120 seconds with exceeding the 180-second restart limit.
"Schema changes with indexes are exactly the new orders work landing now" invents the new migration's contents.
"A Job doesn't [get killed mid-migration]" overstates protection beyond removal of the server liveness probe.
R08.note: It explains the timeout mechanism but invents the current change's contents and overstates both risk frequency and Job guarantees.

errors: "All 3 pods blocked on the lock" is inaccurate: one pod applies the migration while the other two wait.
"Runs the migration once to completion" implies successful completion without stating failure handling.
"No probe kills on index builds" requires configuring the Job without the server liveness probe and does not address other termination causes.
R09.note: It is concise and grounded in the incident, but misdescribes which pods hold versus wait on the lock.

errors: "A slow migration can no longer take the orders API down" overstates protection against database disruption.
"39 ... under 5 seconds" is not established.
"Got killed again" adds an explicit repeated killing not stated in the incident facts.
"It will happen again" asserts certainty about future slow index migrations.
"Nothing kills the migration partway through" is an unsupported guarantee.
"deploy.yml fails with the Job's logs" invents pipeline failure and log behavior.
"Which we can't reliably [predict]" asserts a capability limitation not established by the evidence.
"The cheaper alternative" lacks a verified cost comparison.
R10.note: It usefully states the old-code compatibility assumption, but surrounds that caution with absolute promises and invented pipeline behavior.
